correctness.rationale: On a regular curve, the motivating paper explicitly invokes \(\mathcal{CR}(f)=\mathrm{NW}(f)\). Finite chain recurrence therefore gives finite non-wandering set. Nondegeneracy of the continuum forces a point outside that finite set, hence a wandering point. The regular-curve paper then gives \(h_{pol}(f)=1\), \(h_{pol}(F_n(f))=n\), and \(h_{pol}(2^f)=+\infty\). The symmetric-product-suspension paper gives \(h_{pol}(\mathcal{S}F_n^{m}(f))=h_{pol}(F_n(f))=n h_{pol}(f)\) for every \(n>m\ge1\), with \(m=1\) yielding the ordinary suspension. Hypotheses and quantifiers match exactly; no experiment is used.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification across the induced hyperspace hierarchy for a standard one-dimensional continuum class: every finite particle/quotient level has the exact integer complexity \(n\), independent of the collapsed level \(m\), while the unrestricted hyperspace jumps to infinite polynomial entropy. It joins two recent theories at precisely their common finite-chain-recurrent regular-curve regime and clarifies the finite-versus-infinite complexity boundary; it is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a table recomputation.
